en: {count, plural, one {# message from you since this was asked (last {time})} other {# messages from you since this was asked (last {time})}}
ur: {count, plural, one {اس سوال کے بعد آپ کا # پیغام (آخری {time})} other {اس سوال کے بعد آپ کے # پیغامات (آخری {time})}}

context.note: The line under an OPEN ask's state line on the phone, stating how stale the question is: e.g. '3 messages from you since this was asked (last 19:36)'. {count} is an integer >= 1 (the card draws no line at all for 0 or when an older runtime sends no count) and feeds the plural with `#`; {time} is an ALREADY-FORMATTED 24-hour local clock time (HH:MM) supplied by the caller — do not reformat, translate or wrap it in ICU date syntax. Both plural arms must be complete sentences because some languages reorder the parenthetical time; keep the parentheses and their wording inside each arm. It wraps onto more than one line on a narrow phone, so short words and a natural break after 'asked' are welcome.

context.role: phone ask card, dismiss reason button
context.note: One of the two reason buttons on an OPEN ask's card on the phone, revealed by 'close…'. It means the operator already answered the question by typing in the conversation, so the agent should read their messages and treat the ask as settled (sent as reason=answered_in_chat). A reason, not a command; no exclamation mark. The buttons sit side by side, so keep it short. WIDTH, corrected after the first independent audit: the two reason controls and their cancel are a FLEX-WRAP row (the phone wraps them to separate lines rather than truncating), and the terminal draws the label and its note on ONE row clipped against the list's width — so 34 cells for a label and 44 for a note is the honest budget, and 'conversation'/'conversación'/'cuộc trò chuyện' fit it where a shorter synonym would have had to be invented.

context.note: The one-line explanation drawn UNDER the 'Answered in chat' reason button on the phone, in a smaller dim register. It names what the operator already did, so they can recognise their own case and cannot mistake the button for 'send my answer'. No trailing punctuation, no em dash (the layout puts it on its own line).

A reason, not a command, and it must not read as an approval or a refusal of the question. The buttons sit side by side, so keep it short. WIDTH, corrected after the first independent audit: the two reason controls and their cancel are a FLEX-WRAP row (the phone wraps them to separate lines rather than truncating), and the terminal draws the label and its note on ONE row clipped against the list's width — so 34 cells for a label and 44 for a note is the honest budget, and 'conversation'/'conversación'/'cuộc trò chuyện' fit it where a shorter synonym would have had to be invented.

context.role: phone ask card, dismiss reason note
context.note: The one-line explanation drawn UNDER the 'No longer needed' reason button on the phone, in a smaller dim register. It says what happens to the waiting: the agent stops expecting an answer. No trailing punctuation, no em dash (the layout puts it on its own line), and it must not read as an approval or a refusal of the question itself.

context.role: phone ask card, dismiss control label
context.note: The quiet control on an OPEN ask's card on the phone that reveals the two reasons for putting the question away. It closes the QUESTION, not the screen: keep the trailing ellipsis glyph (…), which is the card's own convention for 'this opens a choice', and keep it lower-case and brief. Use the same verb the terminal uses for this act (dismiss) rather than a second word for it. Nothing is sent until a reason is chosen.

ur: ختم کر دیا گیا — کوئی جواب نہیں بھیجا

context.note: The line the asks sheet shows in place of its empty state after a TIMED-OUT ask was dismissed with the card's one-tap control, which carries no reason. Say that the dismissal was recorded and that no reply was sent to the agent — the lapsed door's own promise. Past tense, no exclamation mark. WIDTH: 44 cells, the widest receipt line any shipped locale needs (Spanish 42, Vietnamese 44); it is a whole sentence on its own row, not a label sharing a control.
